notes: Third Lean round (2026-11-04): the last open Nagao Lemma 4 cell is proved; six protocol-layer overbroad claims are refuted or bounded; a derived claim from WEAKNESS_TRIAGE W7 is withdrawn and recorded as an open lead. Lean modules NagaoLiteralInside.lean and ProtocolCountermodels.lean in research/ecdlp_weakness_lean_20261104/lean.

nodes.label: Nagao Lemma 4 holds in the literal >=, field-equations-inside cell (Lean)
nodes.statement: For every finite family F and every finite family E of field equations over a field, with falls read literally (max deg(g_i G_i) >= d) and the fake degree taken as the least total degree in the class modulo <E>, every fake fall of F u E at degree d is a true fall of F u E at degree d. Hence d_F <= d'_F whenever a fake fall exists.
nodes.scope: Settles the fourth (reading x placement) cell; the other three are refuted (CEX-NAGAO-LEMMA4-F2 and the boundaries table). 'Degree after reduction' is read as the least degree of a representative modulo the field equations, which for <x_j^2 - x_j> is the degree of the multilinear normal form. Does not rescue Nagao's complexity estimates, which need the equality reading.
assumptions: Field equations inside the generating set

formal.notes: Compiled locally with lake env lean -o against Mathlib v4.34.1; AxiomAudit clean. Repository proof gate runs on main after merge.

nodes.label: 'Special soundness implies Fiat-Shamir security'
nodes.statement: Overbroad claim: a special-sound Sigma protocol made non-interactive with any challenge function is a secure proof or signature.
nodes.scope: Refuted with a constant-zero challenge oracle. The Fiat-Shamir theorem needs a random oracle (or equivalent) and domain separation.

nodes.label: Constant-zero challenge: (sP, 0, s) verifies for every key (Lean)
nodes.statement: In any additive group, with challenge oracle H = 0 the Schnorr transcript (R, c, s) = (s P, 0, s) satisfies s P = R + c X for every public key X; no witness is used.

nodes.label: 'Pedersen commitments with independent generators are binding unconditionally'
nodes.statement: Overbroad claim: in a cyclic group, 'independent' generators G, H make m G + r H binding regardless of what is known about log_G H.
nodes.scope: Refuted: a known relation H = t G gives a second opening. Binding is computational and reduces to DLP.

nodes.label: H = tG gives commit(m, r) = commit(m + t, r - 1) (Lean)
nodes.statement: For any module over a commutative ring, m G + r (t G) = (m + t) G + (r - 1)(t G).
nodes.scope: Algebraic identity; distinct openings when t != 0.

nodes.label: 'Cofactor clearing maps onto the prime subgroup bijectively'
nodes.statement: Overbroad claim: multiplying by the cofactor h always acts as a bijection on the prime-order subgroup.
nodes.scope: Refuted when r | h (r^2 | #G); true when r does not divide h.

nodes.label: In Z/9, cofactor 3 kills the order-3 subgroup; coprime cofactors are bijective (Lean)
nodes.statement: Multiplication by 3 sends the order-3 subgroup {0, 3, 6} of Z/9 to 0; on Z/r with r prime, multiplication by any h != 0 is a bijection.
nodes.scope: Group-theoretic countermodel and repair; curve instances need r^2 | #E for the failure.

nodes.label: A nondegenerate pairing decides DDH with one evaluation (Lean)
nodes.statement: For a symmetric bilinear pairing on a one-dimensional space over a field with e(P, P) != 0, e(aP, bP) = e(P, cP) iff c = ab.
nodes.scope: Shows DDH is easy in groups with a nondegenerate self-pairing, independent of the cost of CDH or DLP there; does not prove CDH hard anywhere.

nodes.label: 'Blinding by any group element preserves a subgroup DLP instance'
nodes.statement: Overbroad claim: random self-reduction may blind the target with a random element of the whole group.
nodes.scope: Refuted in Z/2 x Z/3; blinding inside the prime-order subgroup is a bijection.

nodes.label: Ambient blinding leaves the subgroup; subgroup blinding is a bijection (Lean)
nodes.statement: In Z/2 x Z/3 some subgroup element plus some ambient element leaves the order-3 subgroup; in Z/r, a -> q + a is a bijection.

nodes.label: 'Complete, zero-knowledge protocols are sound'
nodes.statement: Overbroad claim: completeness together with zero knowledge gives soundness.
nodes.scope: Refuted by the always-accept protocol for any language with a false statement.

nodes.label: Always-accept protocol: complete, simulatable, unsound (Lean)
nodes.statement: The verifier that accepts every statement accepts every true statement and some false statement whenever the language has one.
nodes.scope: Abstracted to verdicts; zero knowledge is immediate since transcripts carry nothing.

nodes.label: Can a trace-pulled-back subspace factor base be small?
nodes.statement: Base-change E/F_p to F_{p^n}; let F' be the points with x-coordinate in an F_p-subspace V, decompose targets of E(F_p) over F' by Weil descent, and pull relations back with the trace (nR = sum Tr(P_i)). Is there a V for which the pulled-back factor base Tr(F') has size at most p^(1/2 - eps) while targets still decompose with non-negligible probability?
nodes.scope: Replaces a derived claim withdrawn on 2026-11-04 (WEAKNESS_TRIAGE W7): the dimension count bounds |F'| >= p^(dim V), not |Tr(F')|, and the trace map on points is many-to-one. Generic V is expected to give |Tr(F')| near #E(F_p); no argument here rules out special V.

edges.statement: Lemma 4 holds in the literal >=, inside cell for every system; the refutation stands in the other three cells.
Constant-zero challenges accept witness-free transcripts for every key.
The random-oracle premise is load-bearing: without it the verification equation is satisfied with no witness.
A known relation H = tG yields a second opening.
Cofactor 3 annihilates the order-3 subgroup of Z/9.
Cofactor clearing preserves the prime subgroup only when r does not divide h.
DDH is decided by one pairing evaluation, independent of CDH/DLP cost.
The decision reduction in its simplest nondegenerate form, kernel-checked.
Ambient blinding leaves the designated subgroup.
Self-reduction must blind inside the prime subgroup, where blinding is a bijection.
The always-accept protocol is complete and simulatable but unsound.
The subspace mechanism is not excluded on prime fields by a dimension count once relations are pulled back by the trace.
